title: Equinix filed the wrong document to FERC - then asked for mercy in the biggest data-center docket
dek: A procedural comedy with real stakes: Equinix's protest of PJM's large-load plan missed the deadline because it uploaded PJM's own filing instead of its response. Now it is asking to be heard out of time.
body_html:
At 4:20pm on 3 September, forty minutes before the comment deadline in ER26-3515, Equinix submitted what it thought was its protest of PJM's Interim Resource Adequacy Service. What it actually uploaded was a copy of PJM's own filing. FERC Online bounced it - the document carried FERC watermarks - and the corrected version only landed at 10:40pm, after the 5pm cutoff.

This motion asks the Commission to accept the late protest anyway. FERC routinely grants out-of-time motions where the error is clerical, the delay is hours not days, and no party is prejudiced - and Equinix has a timestamped 4:13pm save to prove the real document existed before the deadline. Expect it to be granted.

Why it is more than a blooper

Equinix operates more data centers than anyone else in this fight. Its substantive protest - now attached to this motion - is one of the few operator-side documents in the docket, alongside Google and the Data Center Coalition. If the IMM's attack on IRAS is the prosecution's case, Equinix's corrected filing is part of the defense: operators want interconnection certainty and curtailment credit, not a capacity tax. The wrong-PDF episode delayed that voice by a news cycle, not more.
key_points: Equinix uploaded PJM's own IRAS filing instead of its protest; FERC Online rejected it for watermarks at the deadline.
Corrected protest filed 10:40pm, 5h40m late, with a 4:13pm save timestamp as evidence.
Out-of-time acceptance is routine for clerical errors of hours with no prejudice to other parties.
The underlying protest matters: Equinix is the largest operator voice in the PJM large-load docket.
watch: The Commission's short order granting (or, unlikely, denying) the out-of-time motion.
The substance of Equinix's corrected protest once accepted - especially anything on curtailment credit.

deep_dives.title: How FERC eFiling actually fails
deep_dives.body_html: eLibrary submissions are PDF uploads checked against docket rules. FERC Online's systems stamp received documents with watermarks; uploading an already-stamped document (like a copy of someone else's filing) triggers exactly the rejection Equinix hit. The 5pm cutoff is a server timestamp, which is why the 4:13pm local save time matters for the equity argument but not for the deadline itself.
